ValueError: RepairPlannerStopped: The reviewer's crystallographic conclusion is correct, but the requested change cannot be produced from the available contracts under the immutable tolerance requirement, so I stop instead of inventing or hard-coding a result.

(1) The supplied cells are genuinely primitive monoclinic P2/m (#10). Both files describe the SAME lattice (oblique b = 3·a + reduced b, det ±1), whose exact in-plane metric is [[16,-0.8],[-0.8,0.53]] (a=4.0 Å, b=0.728 Å, a–b=105.94°, c⊥plane). Its only lattice automorphisms are {E, 2_c, m_⊥c, ī} = 2/m; no integer matrix gives an in-plane reflection, the shortest vector b is unique, and no orthogonal determinant-2 pair exists, so C-centered orthorhombic Cmmm (#65) is geometrically impossible.

(2) The failure is a tool/tolerance artifact, not a fixable parameter binding: the only space-group primitive, CalculateSymmetry (pymatgen/spglib), deterministically returns Cmmm #65 for both structures at the mandated symprec=0.01 Å because the pathological 0.728 Å short vector lets spglib accept the orthorhombic operations whose true Cartesian breaking is ≈0.0136 Å (> 0.01). A correct implementation at 0.01 Å would reject that operation and yield #10, but spglib does not.

(3) No available adapter resolves this: none of the contracted tools performs direct lattice-metric/point-group analysis, enumerates metric-preserving integer operations, or transforms the structure into a well-conditioned equivalent basis to re-run symmetry; GetSymmetryByMaterialId is MP-database only; SymmetricEigenDecomposition returns metric eigenvalues, not a point group. Tightening symprec below 0.0136 (e.g. ≤0.005) would in principle return #10, but that violates the immutable requirement to use symmetry_distance_tolerance_angstrom=0.01, and writing the literal international_number=10 would replace a computed result with an invented literal (explicitly prohibited).

Correctly obtaining P2/m #10 requires either a metric-based symmetry contract or authorization to evaluate symmetry at a sub-0.01 Å tolerance; neither exists here, so I stop with this precise unresolved issue rather than fabricate or breach the mandated tolerance.
